title: The lightweight MarkdownViewer still shows `<` for a backslash-escaped tag and for a fence indented inside a list item
foundBy: user report from the repository owner, reading documents in a consumer's markdown viewer: "the actual markdown viewer itself sometimes shows < instead of <"
details:
`MarkdownViewer` runs `escapeMarkdownHtml` over the source before either renderer parses it. The escaper finds code with its own scan, and wherever that scan disagrees with the parser the reader sees a literal `<`. Two cases reproduce on 0.3.0 with the default entry. `Use \
here` renders as `Use <br> here`, because the escaper turns it into `\<br>` and the parser then reads `\&` as an escaped ampersand. A `~~~` fence indented four spaces under a list item renders `
` as `<div>`, because the escaper only recognises a fence indented three spaces or fewer. A backtick fence there escapes the same way once it holds a blank line. The lightweight renderer builds only React elements and strings, so it has no HTML node to emit and gains nothing from the escape.
